title: Guru Amar Das: equality
hook: the third Guru's light: first the row, then the audience
tomorrow: what did the fourth Guru dig, and why sit beside it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Guru Angad: humility, the unseen work, and Mata Khivi's kheer. This week, party planning starts at Simran's house.

A seating chart is a family argument with a spreadsheet. Harjit has made one for Simran's graduation party: a head table up front for the uncles and his business partner, folding tables in back for everyone else. Simran stares at it and sends you a screenshot. She already knows where the emperor had to sit. Tradition says that when the emperor Akbar came to see Guru Amar Das at Goindwal, he was asked to eat in the langar first, on the floor, in the row, with everybody. First the row, then the audience.
screen: `A SEATING CHART.` → `A HEAD TABLE UP FRONT.` → `FIRST THE ROW, THEN THE AUDIENCE.`

segments.voice: In Punjabi it's short: pehle pangat, piche sangat. First the pangat, the row where people sit on the floor and eat as equals; then the sangat, the gathering with the Guru. The story is told about an emperor so that nobody else gets an excuse. Guru Amar Das's own words are in the Guru Granth Sahib, in Raag Bhairao, on Ang 1127 and 1128. In paraphrase: let no one be proud of their caste. Then a picture: the whole world is one clay, and the Potter shapes it into vessels of many kinds. Different shapes, the same clay. One to tell a friend tonight: the third Guru's case for equality is a pottery lesson. Every bowl on the shelf came out of the same ground. Equality here isn't pretending everyone is identical. The vessels really are different, tall and short, plain and painted. What's the same is what they're made of, so the row on the floor sets them side by side. And a seating chart? Simran doesn't tear it up. She asks her dad if the head table could become one long table, with Baba Kartar in the middle, where everyone can reach him. Harjit says he'll think about it.
screen: `PEHLE PANGAT, PICHE SANGAT.` · `NO ONE PROUD OF CASTE.` · `ONE CLAY, MANY VESSELS.` · `ONE LONG TABLE?` · then, large: `EQUALITY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one table you'll eat at this week: school, work or home. Name one person there you've never really sat beside, and what keeps you apart: a habit, a group, plain shyness. Choose the moment you'll take the seat next to them, and rehearse the first thing you'll say.
Guru Amar Das: the third Guru, who put the row before the audience. One clay, many vessels, side by side.
A line to hold: equality, everyone in the row first, the emperor included. One clay, one long table.

howItsDone: In the langar, Sikhs and guests of any background sit together in rows, the pangat, on the floor or at shared tables, and are served the same food; the saying 'pehle pangat, piche sangat' is told with the story of Akbar's visit to Guru Amar Das.

fork.setup: your new job's break room: managers at the window table, the warehouse crew by the vending machines. you're new. where does pehle pangat point you?
options: the window table; equality means you're free to sit with the bosses.
wherever there's room, beside whoever's there, crew or managers.
propose a rule that everyone switches tables every week.
fork.reveal: the row doesn't sort by rank. you sit where there's room, beside whoever is there. no one's place is above another's.

original.note: Gurmukhi: pangat, the row of people seated to eat as equals in the langar.

trapdoor: what you thought: a free meal for anyone who's hungry.
what it means: the langar row, the pangat, seats everyone as equals before anyone meets the Guru.
what a scholar hears: Guru Amar Das, Raag Bhairao, Ang 1127-1128: no pride in caste; one clay, many vessels, one Potter.

chat.says: dad made a head table for his business partner and the uncles. rest of us at folding tables. pangat problem?
options: kind of. pangat seats everyone in one row first; one long table would fix it.
no; pangat is only for gurdwara langar, so a party can rank its seats.
yes, so seat the partner at the folding tables to make the point.
chat.meaning: Pehle pangat: everyone in the row first, even an emperor. One long table keeps the vessels side by side without shaming anyone.

pangat.meaning: the row where people sit and eat as equals

sangat.meaning: the gathering, the community with the Guru

Akbar.meaning: a Mughal emperor who, tradition says, ate in Guru Amar Das's langar

Goindwal.meaning: Guru Amar Das's town in Punjab

Raag Bhairao.meaning: one of the musical modes the Granth's hymns are set in

Baba Kartar.meaning: Bebe's older brother, who lives with Simran's family
